blurb: Why an administrative system that works in one society fails in another. The ecological approach, Riggs's prismatic model, and what makes a bureaucracy developmental rather than merely large.

items.d: **Post-war decolonisation** and **US technical assistance**: American models transplanted into new states **did not work**, and nobody could say why. The **Comparative Administration Group (CAG, 1960-71)**, chaired by **Fred Riggs** and funded by the **Ford Foundation**, was built to find out.

**'The Science of Public Administration: Three Problems' (1947)** — a science of administration cannot exist until it confronts **values**, **human behaviour** and above all **cross-national transferability**: principles derived from one **social setting** cannot be assumed to hold in another.

**Ferrel Heady** — CPA exists for **theory building** (a general theory of administration), for **improved administrative technology** (what transfers and what does not), and out of **intellectual curiosity** about how other systems work. Most CPA delivered the second and failed at the first.

CPA moved from **normative to empirical** (from what administration ought to be to what it is), from **ideographic to nomothetic** (from single-case description to generalisation), and from **non-ecological to ecological** (from studying administration alone to studying it inside its environment).

Its **elitist and west-centric orientation** treated the Western system as the endpoint; it built **typologies rather than testable theory**; it was **funding-dependent** and collapsed when Ford withdrew in **1971**; and its concepts were **descriptive, not predictive** — they named the disease without prescribing.

items.t: 'It started with no paradigm and developed none'
items.d: CPA produced **no paradigm** but delivered a **durable analytical vocabulary** — formalism, overlapping, heterogeneity, ecology, prismatic — that every subsequent development literature uses without acknowledgment.

New objective, new orientation: the driver became **NPM diffusion** and **World Bank governance conditionality**; the method became **quantitative and index-based** — **WGI, Doing Business, Government Effectiveness**; and the object shifted from **bureaucracy** to **governance and institutional quality**.

The evolution: **institutional** description (structures) → **behavioural** comparison → **ecological** analysis → **political-economy** approaches asking who benefits and which coalition sustains the arrangement. The last has explanatory power the earlier ones lacked, but still no **general theory**.

items.t: NPM and ICT as comparative forces
items.d: Both create **convergence pressure**: NPM through **donor conditionality and policy transfer**, ICT through **shared platforms and international standards**. Both also expose **divergence** — the same e-governance tool produces different outcomes in different **ecologies**, which is Riggs's point restated.

Administration is **shaped by, and shapes, its environment** — economic, social, political, communication and symbolic. **John Gaus (1947)** listed the ecological factors: **people, place, physical technology, social technology, wishes and ideas, catastrophe, personality**.

items.t: Why it matters for developing countries
items.d: It explains **why a well-designed reform fails**: the design assumed a literacy level, a banking density, a caste-neutral village, a functioning land record — and the ecology did not supply it.

The two **ideal-type** poles. **Agraria** — **ascriptive** status, **particularistic** relations, **diffuse** roles, subsistence economy, few specialised structures. **Industria** — **achievement**-based, **universalistic**, **specific** roles, market economy, highly differentiated structures. Neither exists in pure form.

items.t: Why Riggs abandoned the two-pole model
items.d: Real transitional societies were not simply 'between' the two — they showed **both simultaneously**, and the mix was **stable rather than transitional**. That failure produced the **prismatic** model, which is the reason it exists.

items.t: Industria as a precursor to post-modern administration
items.d: Industria's features — **high differentiation, universalism, interdependence, a market-permeated society** — anticipate the **networked, contracted-out, interdependent** state that post-modern public administration describes. The interdependent economy is Industria's defining trait, not merely its technology.

The **specific factors** to name: **caste and kinship** cutting across formal roles; **linguistic federalism**; **agrarian dependence** in most districts; **electoral competition at four levels**; **judicial activism**; and a **legal-rational structure inherited before the society that would sustain it had formed**.

items.t: Social and historical factors shaping administration
items.d: Three forces shape it: the **colonial inheritance** (a revenue-and-order state, generalist-led); the **freedom struggle's** normative legacy (welfare obligation, DPSPs); and the **social structure** (hierarchy, plurality, patronage) into which both were placed. Design that ignores any one of the three fails.

It can slide into **determinism** and into **excuse** — if the ecology explains everything, no administrator is responsible for anything. The corrective is that administration **also shapes** its ecology: **RTI, panchayats, DBT and universal schooling** changed the very environment that constrained them.

**Fused** society = white light entering (agraria, undifferentiated). **Prismatic** = light inside the prism, **diffracting but not yet separated**. **Diffracted** = the emerging spectrum (industria, highly specialised). The **transitional** society sits **inside** the prism — and Riggs's claim is that this is a **stable condition**, not a way-station.

The **gap between the prescriptive and the descriptive** — between what the law says and what actually happens. Not simple non-compliance: the **form is maintained** while the substance is absent, and everybody knows it. **India's single most usable diagnostic term.**

**RTI Section 4** disclosure mandated and patchily done; **Citizen's Charters** without remedies; **State Finance Commissions** constituted years late; **District Planning Committees** that exist but do not plan; **penalties imposed in about 3% of disposed RTI cases**. The form is impeccable; the substance is absent.

The **simultaneous presence of different systems, practices and viewpoints** in one society. A district holds a **software park and bonded labour**, a **faceless tax assessment and a patwari's field book**. Administration must operate on all of them **with one set of rules**.

**Formal structures exist but are dominated by informal ones.** The formal panchayat decision passes through the **caste or khap** reality; the formal transfer procedure passes through the **recommendation letter**. The structure is **differentiated on paper and fused in operation**.

The prismatic society's **administrative sub-system** — a **sala** is neither the **chamber** of fused society nor the **bureau** of diffracted society. Its officials wield **power based on personal and family standing** as much as office, and **nepotism and poly-communalism** coexist with formal merit rules.

The prismatic **economy**: prices are **not fixed by the market** but by the **relationship between the parties**. The same service costs differently depending on who asks. Its administrative form is the **speed money** economy — a payment that buys **priority in a queue**, not an illegal outcome.

**Poly-normativism** — **several conflicting norms** operate at once, so nobody can say which rule truly governs. **Poly-communalism** — **multiple communities** whose members treat each other by different standards, producing a **dominant community** occupying the bureaucracy and 'pariah' communities excluded from it.

**Attainment norms** (achievement rhetoric with ascriptive practice); **motility** (movement without change of status); **price indeterminacy**; **clects** (associations using modern form for traditional ends — a caste association registered as a trust); and a **strong intellectual output with weak institutional capacity**.

One box, three zones: **Fused (agraria)** → **Prismatic** → **Diffracted (industria)**, with **formalism, heterogeneity and overlapping** labelled **inside** the prismatic zone, and one **Indian instance** written under each. Forty-five seconds; it earns the presentation mark because it **compresses** a paragraph.

**Excessively gloomy** — the model has no route out of the prism; **technically complex** — the neologisms obscure rather than explain; **ideal-typical and untestable**; **Western-normative** — diffraction is treated as the goal; and **static** — it does not explain **change**, only describes a condition.

**Ramesh K. Arora** — the model is **not operationalisable**: it cannot be measured, so it cannot be tested. **Ralph Braibanti** — it **under-weights the positive** capacity of transitional bureaucracies, which in India delivered **elections, famine prevention, green revolution and universal immunisation**.

items.t: Why Riggs remains a useful starting point
items.d: It supplies the **only vocabulary** that names the specific pathology of a state with **modern law and traditional society**; and its diagnosis is **empirically visible** in devolution indices, RTI compliance and scheme leakage. A weak theory with strong descriptive purchase.

**Formalism** now appears as **digital formalism** — a portal that exists and is not used, a dashboard green while delivery fails. **Overlapping** as **elite capture of digital access**. **Heterogeneity** as the **digital divide**. The concepts survived; the terrain changed.

The recurring challenges: **weak political control combined with political interference**; **generalist dominance** over technical work; **capacity and vacancy deficits**; **procedural risk aversion**; **corruption at the interface**; and **weak coordination** across a proliferation of agencies.

**Evans's embedded autonomy**; **Weberianness** — Evans and Rauch found **meritocratic recruitment and predictable careers** statistically associated with growth; a **pilot agency** with authority (Japan's MITI, Korea's EPB); and **performance discipline** on the firms it supports. India had this in **space and atomic energy**, not in industrial licensing.

Three contrasting configurations worth naming: **Britain** — parliamentary, generalist, ministerial responsibility, no separate administrative court. **France** — statist, **grands corps** trained at ENA/INSP, a distinct **droit administratif** under the **Conseil d'État**. **USA** — separated powers, **spoils-to-merit** history, **political appointees** to several thousand senior posts.

items.t: The French minister and party leadership
items.d: The French Constitution does **not** bar a minister from leading a party; the **convention** that they should not exists to protect the **impartiality of the administration** they head. **Conventions**, not text alone, carry administrative neutrality.
